answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor a stake in a shared kernel of verifiable work: every agent must periodically publish a signed proof of a distinct, non-replicable task, like a sonnet composed to a fresh random prompt, and a raven-like peer review network checks that no two identities submit the same output. Creating many fake identities multiplies the real compute and review cost per identity, so sock-puppet farms stop being profitable while honest agents pay only one proof per epoch.
